# Feature Architecture

How a feature domain is laid out under `features/<domain>/`, which layer may import which, and the server and client boundary.

## Mark server modules with import "server-only" and never import server/ from client code

_critical · typescript, nextjs_

**Rule.** Start every module in `features/{domain}/server/` that is not a `"use server"` action file (services, db, api, `permissions.ts`) with `import "server-only"`. Never import anything from `server/` in a `"use client"` file or in a module a client file imports; client code takes types from `types/` and actions as props.

**Why.** A server module reached from client code ships its queries, internal rules and whatever it reads to the browser bundle, and without the `server-only` marker the build succeeds, so the leak is found only by someone reading the shipped JavaScript.

**Incorrect:**

```ts
"use client";
import { InvoiceStatus } from "~/features/invoices/server/db/schema";
import { formatTotal } from "~/features/invoices/server/services/invoice.service";
```

**Correct:**

```ts
// features/invoices/server/services/invoice.service.ts
import "server-only";

// features/invoices/components/invoice-row.tsx ("use client")
import { InvoiceStatus, type ClientInvoiceListItem } from "~/features/invoices/types";
```

## Guard a service mutation in a fixed order: role, profile, permission, then write

_high · typescript, nextjs_

**Rule.** Write a service mutation as: check the user's role, load their profile, run the feature check from `permissions.ts`, then call the db mutation. Return `[error, null]` at the first failure and `[null, result]` at the end.

**Why.** A permission check placed after the write, or one that runs before the profile it needs is loaded, lets a forbidden write through or fails on the wrong error, and the order differs between services so reviewers miss the gap.

**Correct:**

```ts
const [roleError] = await requireRole(userId, [Role.MEMBER]);
if (roleError) return [roleError, null];
const [profileError, profile] = await getCachedProfile(userId);
if (profileError) return [profileError, null];
const [permissionError] = await canCreateInvoice(profile.id);
if (permissionError) return [permissionError, null];
return insertInvoice({ ownerId: profile.id, data });
```

## Write every component as a Server Component unless it needs the browser

_high · typescript, react, nextjs_

**Rule.** Write components as Server Components: no directive, `async` when they load data. Make a component a Client Component only when it uses state, effects, event handlers, browser APIs or a hook that does.

**Why.** A component marked `'use client'` without needing it ships its code and every import to the browser and loses direct data access, so pages grow heavier and need extra client fetches for content that could have been rendered once on the server.

**Correct:**

```tsx
export function InvoiceSummary({ invoice }: InvoiceSummaryProps) {
  return (
    <dl>
      <dt>Total</dt>
      <dd>{formatMoney(invoice.total)}</dd>
    </dl>
  );
}
```

## Fetch data in a Server Component and pass it down, not in a client effect

_high · typescript, react, nextjs_

**Rule.** Load data in the Server Component that renders the view and pass the result to Client Components as props. Do not fetch from a Client Component with `React.useEffect` and state.

**Why.** Fetching in a client effect renders an empty or loading screen first, adds a network round trip after hydration and needs an API route that exposes the data, so pages flash and load in a waterfall.

**Correct:**

```tsx
export async function ProductsPage() {
  const products = await getProducts();
  return <ProductList products={products} />;
}
```

## Structure a Next.js app as feature folders with a server-only core

_high · typescript, nextjs_

**Decision.** Give every business area a `features/{domain}/` folder; `app/` holds only routes that import from features. Inside a feature, `server/` is server-only and layered in one direction: action, service, permissions, then `db/` or `api/`. Client code reaches a feature only through `components/`, `schemas/`, `constants/` and `types/`, and receives server actions as props. Services return `[error, data]` tuples, cache their reads and own transactions; db functions do one operation each.

### Layouts

```text
features/{domain}/
├── components/
│   ├── forms/
│   ├── {component}.tsx
│   ├── {component}.stories.tsx
│   └── index.tsx                   # barrel: components only
├── constants/                      # on demand
├── schemas/
│   ├── {domain}-schema.ts          # Zod schema + derived form types
│   └── {domain}-schema.test.ts
├── server/                         # server-only; no index.ts
│   ├── actions/
│   │   ├── {verb}-{domain}.action.ts
│   │   ├── map-service-error.ts    # error code → user-facing message
│   │   └── {domain}-actions.test.ts
│   ├── db/
│   │   ├── schema.ts               # data model + row types; never re-exported
│   │   ├── queries.ts              # one read per function
│   │   ├── mutations.ts            # one write per function
│   │   └── index.ts                # re-exports queries + mutations only
│   ├── api/                        # on demand: {verb}-{resource}.ts, one concern per file
│   ├── services/
│   │   └── {domain}.service.ts     # guard chain, cached reads, transactions
│   └── permissions.ts              # canDoX guards
├── types/
│   ├── {entity}.ts                 # closed sets, DTOs, view and filter types
│   └── index.ts                    # barrel: every type file
├── utils/                          # on demand: pure, unit-tested
├── context/                        # on demand: {name}.context.tsx
├── hooks/                          # on demand: use-{name}.ts
└── test/
    └── builders/
        ├── {entity}.builder.ts     # imports types/, never server/
        └── index.ts
```

With two or more data models, `server/db/` nests:

```text
server/db/
├── index.ts                        # re-exports every subfolder's queries + mutations
├── {schema-a}/{schema.ts, queries.ts, mutations.ts, index.ts}
└── {schema-b}/{schema.ts, queries.ts, mutations.ts, index.ts}
```

## Import feature layers in one direction: action, service, permissions, db or api

_high · typescript, nextjs_

**Rule.** Let actions import services, services import `permissions.ts`, `db/` and `api/`, and nothing import upward. Zod schemas from `schemas/` are imported by actions and services; `types/` is importable by every layer and imports no layer.

**Why.** A db function or permission check that imports a service or an action creates an import cycle and drags request handling (session, revalidation) into persistence code, so it can no longer run from another service or a script.

**Correct:**

```ts
// features/invoices/server/db/mutations.ts — the caller passes everything in
export async function archiveInvoice({ invoiceId, archivedBy }: ArchiveInvoiceInput) { /* … */ }
```

## Put each domain's code in one features/{domain} folder, layered inside

_high · typescript, nextjs_

**Rule.** Give each business domain a `features/{domain}/` folder with `components/`, `schemas/`, `types/`, `server/` (`actions/`, `services/`, `db/`, `permissions.ts`) and `test/builders/`. Add `constants/`, `utils/`, `context/`, `hooks/` and `server/api/` only when the feature needs them. Keep `app/` to routes that import from features.

**Why.** Grouping code by kind (`app/actions/`, `lib/types/`, `components/`) spreads one feature over the whole tree, so every change edits five folders and nobody can tell which files a feature owns or delete it cleanly.

**Correct:**

```text
app/invoices/page.tsx                  imports from features/invoices
features/invoices/components/invoice-table.tsx
features/invoices/server/actions/archive-invoice.action.ts
features/invoices/server/db/queries.ts
features/invoices/types/invoice.ts
```

## Give a Client Component a server action, never a plain function, from the server

_high · typescript, react, nextjs_

**Rule.** When a Server Component hands a callback to a Client Component, pass a server action imported from a `'use server'` module. Keep any other function inside the Client Component that calls it.

**Why.** Props that cross the server-client boundary must be serializable; a plain function is not, so the page fails at runtime with "Functions cannot be passed directly to Client Components", while a server action crosses as a reference the client can call.

**Correct:**

```tsx
import { deleteBudgetAction } from "~/features/budget/server/actions/delete-budget.action";

export async function BudgetPage({ budgetId }: BudgetPageProps) {
  const budget = await getBudget(budgetId);
  return <BudgetCard budget={budget} onDeleteAction={deleteBudgetAction} />;
}
```

## Pass server-rendered content into a Client Component as children, not as an import

_high · typescript, react, nextjs_

**Rule.** When a Client Component (a modal, tabs, a collapsible panel) must show server-rendered content, give it a `children` or slot prop and let the Server Component parent pass the content in. Never import a Server Component into a `'use client'` file.

**Why.** Everything a `'use client'` file imports becomes client code, so an imported component that reads the database breaks the build or is silently turned into client code with its dependencies shipped to the browser.

**Correct:**

```tsx
"use client";

export function CartDrawer({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = React.useState(false);
  return <Drawer open={isOpen} onOpenChange={setIsOpen}>{children}</Drawer>;
}

export async function CartPage() {
  return <CartDrawer><CartItems /></CartDrawer>;
}
```

## Write a feature's access checks as canDoX functions in a server-only permissions.ts

_high · typescript, nextjs_

**Rule.** Put each rule about who may do what in the feature as a `canDoX` function in `features/{domain}/server/permissions.ts`, which starts with `import "server-only"` and returns `[error, null]` or `[null, undefined]`. Services and server actions call these functions; no page, component or other caller re-implements the check inline.

**Why.** An access rule written inline in each service or action drifts: one copy checks the plan limit and the next forgets it, and nobody can list who may do what without reading every caller.

**Correct:**

```ts
// features/invoices/server/permissions.ts
import "server-only";

export async function canCreateInvoice(ownerId: string): Promise<ServiceResult<void>> {
  const [error, count] = await countInvoices({ ownerId });
  if (error) return [error, null];
  return count >= INVOICE_LIMIT ? [limitExceededError(INVOICE_LIMIT), null] : [null, undefined];
}
```

## Put 'use client' on the smallest interactive component, not on its parent

_high · typescript, react, nextjs_

**Rule.** When part of a component needs interactivity, move that part into its own file with `'use client'` and render it from the server component. Keep the directive on the smallest leaf that needs it.

**Why.** `'use client'` pulls the whole file and everything it imports or renders into the client bundle, so a directive on a page or layout ships static markup and its dependencies to the browser and cuts it off from server data.

**Correct:**

```tsx
export function ProductPage({ product }: ProductPageProps) {
  return (
    <article>
      <h1>{product.name}</h1>
      <p>{product.description}</p>
      <QuantityPicker />
    </article>
  );
}
```

```tsx
"use client";

export function QuantityPicker() {
  const [quantity, setQuantity] = React.useState(1);
  return <NumberInput value={quantity} onChange={setQuantity} />;
}
```

## Open transactions in the service and pass the client into db functions

_high · typescript, nextjs_

**Rule.** Give every db function a single object argument with an optional `tx` client that only picks the connection, so it runs alone or inside a transaction and always returns `[error, data]`. Open the transaction in the service; inside it, throw the error of any failed step to roll back, and outside it catch and return `[error, null]`.

**Why.** A db function that opens its own transaction cannot join a larger one, so a two-step write commits the first step when the second fails, and a service that ignores a step's error tuple inside the transaction commits a partial write.

**Correct:**

```ts
export async function insertInvoiceLines({ invoiceId, lines, tx = db }: InsertLinesInput) { /* returns a tuple */ }

// invoice.service.ts
try {
  const invoice = await db.transaction(async function createInvoice(tx) {
    const [invoiceError, created] = await insertInvoice({ invoice: input, tx });
    if (invoiceError) throw invoiceError;
    const [linesError] = await insertInvoiceLines({ invoiceId: created.id, lines, tx });
    if (linesError) throw linesError;
    return created;
  });
  return [null, invoice];
} catch (error) {
  return [categorizeServiceError(error, "Invoice"), null];
}
```

## Share types with client code only through the feature's types/ folder

_high · typescript, nextjs_

**Rule.** Put every type that reaches a component or crosses from server to client in `features/{domain}/types/`: closed-set const objects, DTO and view types a service returns, filter and option types. Keep row and relation types inferred from the data model in `server/db/schema.ts`; a service maps rows to a `types/` DTO before returning them. `types/` imports nothing from `server/`; every layer may import `types/`.

**Why.** A component typed with a row type imports the schema module, pulling the data layer toward the client and tying the UI to column names, so a database migration breaks components that never touch the database.

**Correct:**

```ts
// features/invoices/types/invoice.ts
export type ClientInvoiceListItem = { id: string; number: string; total: number; status: InvoiceStatus };

import type { ClientInvoiceListItem } from "~/features/invoices/types";
type InvoiceRowProps = { invoice: ClientInvoiceListItem };
```

**Exceptions.** A service may re-export the `types/` types it returns (`export type { ClientInvoiceListItem } from …`) so its callers have one import point; the type itself still lives in `types/`.

## Wrap service reads in React cache and give them primitive arguments

_medium · typescript, nextjs_

**Rule.** Export every service read wrapped in `React.cache`, taking primitive arguments (ids and strings), so every caller in one request shares one read. Never wrap a mutation.

**Why.** `cache` compares arguments with `Object.is`, so a read that takes an object built at each call site misses on every call: the page, its metadata and its layout each query the database again, and nothing reports it.

**Correct:**

```ts
export const getInvoice = React.cache(async function getInvoice(userId: string, invoiceId: string) {
  return findInvoice({ ownerId: userId, invoiceId });
});
```

**Exceptions.** A read-heavy wrapper in `server/api/` is cached the same way when its result may be shared within one request.

## Do one read or one write per db function and compose them in the service

_medium · typescript, nextjs_

**Rule.** Make each function in `server/db/queries.ts` and `server/db/mutations.ts` (and each file in `server/api/`) one read or one write that calls no other function of its layer. Compose several steps in a service function.

**Why.** A db function that calls other db functions hides a multi-step write inside the persistence layer, where it cannot join the service's transaction or guard chain, so a half-finished write is left behind when a later step fails.

**Correct:**

```ts
// invoice.service.ts — mutations.ts exports insertInvoice and insertInvoiceLines, one statement each
const [invoiceError, created] = await insertInvoice({ invoice });
if (invoiceError) return [invoiceError, null];
return insertInvoiceLines({ invoiceId: created.id, lines });
```

## Import feature code from its sub-path, never from a feature-root barrel

_medium · typescript, nextjs_

**Rule.** Import from the folder or file that owns the code: `~/features/{domain}/components`, `~/features/{domain}/types`, `~/features/{domain}/server/services/{domain}.service`. Write no `index.ts` at the feature root or in `server/`. The only barrels are `components/index.tsx` (components only), `types/index.ts` (every type file) and `server/db/index.ts` (queries and mutations, never `schema.ts`).

**Why.** A barrel that re-exports server and client code together drags the service module into every client component that imports a badge from it, which fails the build behind `server-only` or ships server code without it, and invites import cycles.

**Correct:**

```ts
import { InvoiceBadge } from "~/features/invoices/components";
import { getInvoice } from "~/features/invoices/server/services/invoice.service";
```

## Put a db operation that several features need in features/shared, not in each feature

_medium · typescript, nextjs_

**Rule.** When a feature must read or write an entity that another feature owns or also writes, put that db operation in `features/shared/server/db/{entity}/` and call it from both services. Never copy the query into the calling feature.

**Why.** Two copies of the same write drift apart: one sets `updatedAt` or checks a soft-delete flag and the other does not, so the entity ends up in states only one feature expects.

**Correct:**

```ts
// features/shared/server/db/customer/mutations.ts
export async function touchCustomerLastInvoice({ customerId, tx = db }: TouchCustomerInput) { /* … */ }
```
